TryGetArg.description: Reads one of the action's variables (the %name% words) by its name. The version with a type turns the value into that type for you, like text or a whole number.
TryGetArg.returns: true and the value when the variable exists (and fits the type), otherwise false. Always false while Init() runs outside an action.

SetArgument.description: Sets a variable (a %name% word) for the rest of this action, so later sub-actions can use it. Only works while an action runs, not from Init().

GetSource.description: Tells you which kind of event started this action, like Twitch or Command. Gives None when you ran the action by hand.
GetSource.returns: The event source, or None when it is unknown.

GetEventType.description: Tells you exactly which event started this action, like TwitchFollow or TwitchCheer. Gives None when it is unknown or you ran the action by hand.

LogInfo.description: Writes a normal line to Cuebot's log. Handy to see what your code is doing.

LogWarn.description: Writes a warning line to Cuebot's log. Use it when something looks wrong but your code can go on.
LogWarn.example: CPH.LogWarn("No game name was given, using Just Chatting.");

LogError.description: Writes an error line to Cuebot's log. Use it when something failed.
LogError.example: CPH.LogError("Could not reach the song list.");

LogDebug.description: Writes a debug line to Cuebot's log, for extra details while you test your code.

LogVerbose.description: Writes a very detailed line to Cuebot's log. In Cuebot this is the same as LogDebug.

Wait.description: Pauses your code for a number of milliseconds (1000 = 1 second). It stops early when the action is cancelled or the script runs out of time.

Between.description: Picks a random whole number between two numbers. Both ends can be picked. If you swap them by mistake, it still works.
Between.returns: A random whole number from min to max.
Between.example:
int roll = CPH.Between(1, 6);
CPH.LogInfo($"You rolled a {roll}!");

NextDouble.description: Picks a random number from 0 up to (but not including) 1. Handy for chances, like a 25% win.
NextDouble.returns: A random number from 0 to just under 1.
NextDouble.example:
double chance = CPH.NextDouble();
CPH.LogInfo(chance < 0.25 ? "You win!" : "Try again.");

GetVersion.description: Gives you Cuebot's version number. (Streamer.bot gives its own version; Cuebot gives Cuebot's.)
